food_overview.one_line_description: Hyderabad is India's UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy, home to the legendary Hyderabadi Biryani, Irani Chai culture, Haleem, and a 400-year-old culinary tradition shaped by Nizams, Persians, and Telugu influences.

signature_dishes.context: The crown jewel - fragrant basmati rice layered with marinated meat, slow-cooked in sealed handi since Nizam era
Ramzan special - meat, wheat, and ghee slow-cooked for hours into a silky porridge; Hyderabad's first non-veg GI-tagged dish
Iconic Hyderabad tea culture - thick milky chai with sweet-salty cardamom biscuits named after the last Nizam
Nizam-era mutton cooked on a heated granite stone with minimal spices
Royal apricot dessert stewed in sugar syrup, served with cream - the quintessential Hyderabadi sweet
The holy trinity of Hyderabadi breakfast - rice-dal porridge with minced meat and tangy tamarind chutney
Slow-cooked goat trotter soup enjoyed at dawn with square naan
Hyderabadi bread pudding - fried bread soaked in saffron milk, a wedding staple
Square-shaped Hyderabadi samosa filled with minced meat - a fading Nizam-era snack
Charcoal-grilled minced meat kebabs served with Warqi Paratha

famous_food_quarters.character: 400-year-old food heritage, biryani, haleem, kebabs, Irani cafes, sweet shops
Upscale dining, modern cafes, fine dining, night life
IT corridor, modern chains, food trucks, international cuisine
Heritage eateries, Sindhi Colony food street, original Paradise outlet
Late-night biryani and kebab hub, mandi restaurants

food_culture_notes: Hyderabad was designated India's first UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy in 2019
The city has a stronger culture of biscuits than breads, a legacy of Irani cafes
Mutton biryani is the authentic choice - chicken versions came later
Haleem is only available widely during Ramzan (30-day window); limited places serve it year-round
Always visit the original outlet, not chain branches - quality drops significantly
Old City food trail is walkable (~2 km) and budget-friendly (under Rs 500)
Friday specials include Bagara Khana at Shadab and Shikhampur Kebab at select places
Locals often share tables with strangers - this is normal and part of the culture

street_food_guide.overview: Hyderabad's street food scene is legendary, rooted in 400 years of culinary tradition centered around the Old City near Charminar. From Irani chai at dawn to kebabs at dusk, the area from Charminar to Madina Circle forms a 2-km walkable food trail that captures the soul of the city's food culture. Beyond the Old City, food streets like Sindhi Colony and modern hubs like Gachibowli offer diverse street food experiences.

must_try_street_foods.what_it_is: Thick, velvety tea prepared using the traditional 'dum' process - milk-heavy with a unique creamy texture that defines Hyderabad's tea culture
must_try_street_foods.where_to_find_best: Nimrah Cafe (next to Charminar), Cafe 555 (Masab Tank), Grand Hotel (Abids - since 1935), Alpha Hotel (Secunderabad - since 1957)
must_try_street_foods.safety_note: Safe from established cafes - served boiling hot. Avoid from unknown roadside vendors.

must_try_street_foods.what_it_is: Sweet-salty cardamom biscuits named after the last Nizam, with a buttery-sweet taste and a hint of saltiness at the end - designed to be dunked in Irani chai
must_try_street_foods.where_to_find_best: Nimrah Cafe (Charminar - fresh from the oven), Subhan Bakery (Nampally - eggless, 25% cheaper), Karachi Bakery (Multiple outlets)
must_try_street_foods.price: VERIFY: Rs 5-10 for 2 biscuits; Rs 180-220 for 400g pack
must_try_street_foods.safety_note: Very safe - baked fresh daily at established bakeries. Check for egg if strict vegetarian.

must_try_street_foods.what_it_is: A traditional square-shaped Hyderabadi savory pastry (predating the samosa in the city) filled with spicy minced meat (keema). Called 'chaar koni' (four corners) for its signature shape - the square means more crispy edges
must_try_street_foods.where_to_find_best: Hotel Shahran (Charminar - arrive 4-6 PM, sells out fast), Hotel Nayaab (afternoon/evening), Bismillah Hotel (Chaderghat - only 20-35 pieces made daily)
must_try_street_foods.safety_note: Eat only when freshly fried and hot. Avoid if it has been sitting out - it goes stale quickly.

must_try_street_foods.what_it_is: Nizam-era lamb/mutton delicacy where marinated boneless meat is cooked on a heated granite stone (pahadi stone) with ghee - dating back to the 19th century. The meat literally melts in your mouth with a smoky, rich flavor
must_try_street_foods.where_to_find_best: Bade Miyan Kababs (Necklace Road - THE destination, 4th generation since 1954), Chicha's (Lakdikapul - daily in evenings), Al-Akbar Fast Food (Charminar), Sarvi Restaurant (Banjara Hills)
must_try_street_foods.safety_note: Safe when cooked fresh on the hot stone in front of you. The high cooking temperature kills bacteria.

must_try_street_foods.what_it_is: Spicy goat brain fry - a Hyderabadi delicacy that is soft, intensely flavored, and 'absolutely yummylicious.' Cooked with onions, tomatoes, and Hyderabadi spices
must_try_street_foods.where_to_find_best: Hotel Nayaab (Charminar - the standout preparation since 1986), Chicha's (Lakdikapul), Grand Hotel (Abids)
must_try_street_foods.safety_note: Only eat at busy, established restaurants with high turnover. Avoid at unknown stalls.

must_try_street_foods.what_it_is: A quintessential Hyderabadi side dish - green chillies cooked in a rich peanut-sesame-tamarind gravy. Served alongside biryani as an essential accompaniment, not a standalone dish
must_try_street_foods.where_to_find_best: Hotel Shadab (Charminar), Cafe Bahar (Basheer Bagh), Meridian Restaurant (Panjagutta), Shah Ghouse (Shalibanda)
must_try_street_foods.price: VERIFY: Rs 40-80 per serving (usually included with biryani)
must_try_street_foods.safety_note: Generally safe - cooked at high temperatures. Very spicy - start with a small portion.

must_try_street_foods.what_it_is: THE Hyderabadi dessert - dried apricots stewed in sugar syrup until they become soft and jam-like, served with a dollop of cream or vanilla ice cream. The apricot seeds are crushed and sprinkled on top for crunch
must_try_street_foods.where_to_find_best: Hotel Shadab (Charminar - served with unique unsweetened malai scoops), Pista House (Multiple), Grand Hotel (Abids), most Old City restaurants
must_try_street_foods.safety_note: Very safe - cooked at high temperature and preserved in sugar syrup.

must_try_street_foods.what_it_is: Hyderabadi bread pudding - fried bread slices soaked in saffron-flavored milk and sugar syrup, loaded with khoa (reduced milk solids) and dry fruits. A wedding staple and royal dessert
must_try_street_foods.where_to_find_best: Hameedi Confectioners (Mozam Jahi Market - 125+ years old), Hotel Shadab, Pista House, Grand Hotel
must_try_street_foods.safety_note: Safe from established restaurants. Extremely rich and sweet - share one portion.

must_try_street_foods.what_it_is: Hyderabad's most famous Ramzan special - meat (mutton/chicken), wheat, lentils, and ghee slow-cooked for 6-8 hours until it becomes a silky, porridge-like consistency. Hyderabad's first non-vegetarian GI-tagged dish
must_try_street_foods.where_to_find_best: Pista House (world-famous, most consistent), Shah Ghouse (Shalibanda - legendary), Cafe 555 (award-winning), Sarvi Restaurant (Irani version with extra dry fruits), Hotel Nayaab (first to make it commercially available)
must_try_street_foods.safety_note: Only widely available during Ramzan (30-day window). Outside Ramzan, only select outlets serve it - go to established names. Eat hot and fresh.

must_try_street_foods.what_it_is: Charcoal-grilled minced meat (mutton or beef) kebabs, smoky and juicy, served with Warqi Paratha (multi-layered flaky bread) and khatta (tangy chutney). A quintessential Old City street food experience
must_try_street_foods.where_to_find_best: Kebab-E-Jahangiri (Charminar - 36+ years, beef sheekh kebab), Hotel Shahran (Charminar - mutton sheekh with brilliant peanut chutney), Bade Miyan Kababs (Necklace Road)
must_try_street_foods.price: VERIFY: Rs 40-80 for 4 pieces; full meal under Rs 100
must_try_street_foods.safety_note: Eat from busy stalls with high turnover. Kebabs are grilled fresh on charcoal - the high heat makes them safe. Seating is basic - hygiene may be limited.

street_food_areas.why: The 400-year-old food heartland of Hyderabad. The 2-km radius around Charminar offers the most authentic and diverse street food - from Irani chai and kebabs to biryani and haleem. This is where Nizam-era culinary traditions are still alive. The walkable food trail from Charminar to Madina Circle covers 10+ legendary spots.
street_food_areas.best_time: 6:00-9:00 AM for breakfast (Paya, Nihari, Dosa, Irani Chai); 4:00-9:00 PM for evening kebabs and snacks; Ramzan nights for all-night haleem and special items

street_food_areas.why: One of Hyderabad's oldest and most vibrant food streets on Prenderghast Road. What started with small bandis has transformed into a buzzing hub offering cuisine from across India - desi pizzas, 100+ kulfi varieties, vada pav, chaat, and live dosa counters. Mostly vegetarian-friendly.
street_food_areas.best_time: 5:00 PM - 10:00 PM (evening) - most stalls are closed during the day

street_food_areas.why: Hyderabad's modern IT corridor food scene - a mix of food trucks, trendy cafes, late-night dosa spots, and international street food. Ram Ki Bandi's Hitech City outlet serves until midnight. Good for fusion and contemporary street food options.
street_food_areas.best_time: 7:00 PM - 12:00 AM (late evening and night) - caters to the IT crowd working late hours

street_food_areas.why: A historic market area that is the one-stop destination for desserts and bakery items. Home to Hameedi Confectioners (125+ years, Nizam's favorite Jauzi Halwa), Bilal Ice Cream inside an 80-year-old clock tower, and the legendary Subhan Bakery for fresh Osmania biscuits. Sweet lovers' paradise.
street_food_areas.best_time: 9:00 AM - 10:00 PM - best visited in the evening for desserts after dinner

jain_traveller.situation: Finding strictly Jain food (no onion, garlic, root vegetables) in Hyderabad is manageable but requires planning. Unlike Rajasthan or Gujarat, Hyderabad does not have a strong Jain dining culture, but several excellent dedicated and accommodating options exist. Only one restaurant - Jain Kitchen - offers a full dedicated Jain menu where every item can be prepared Jain-style. Most other 'pure veg' restaurants will accommodate on request but with limited options. The good news is that Satvik (no onion/garlic) restaurants like Sattvam are excellent fallback options.
tips: Jain Kitchen is the ONLY restaurant in Hyderabad with a full dedicated Jain menu - they can convert ANY menu item to Jain preparation (no onion/garlic/potato/cauliflower/carrot/ginger)
Sattvam follows Satvik principles (no onion/garlic) with a 108-item buffet - the best overall choice for Jain travellers seeking variety
Gaurang's Kitchen offers a dedicated Jain thali in an upscale designer setting - great for special occasions
Govinda's Restaurant is ISKCON-affiliated with verified 100% No Onion No Garlic preparation
Rajthali's Rajasthani/Gujarati thali is naturally Jain-friendly and requires minimal modifications
Always explicitly mention 'Jain food' when ordering - most pure veg restaurants understand the requirement
Avoid biryani restaurants entirely - even 'veg biryani' is prepared in the same kitchen as non-veg biryani
Be cautious with street food - cross-contamination risk and unknown ingredients in chutneys
South Indian breakfast items (idli, dosa) at pure veg places are generally safe when specified Jain
Carry Jain snacks for emergencies - options are limited outside the listed restaurants

halal_traveller.situation: Hyderabad is one of India's most halal-friendly cities with a large Muslim population, especially in the Old City around Charminar. Almost all restaurants in Old City, Irani cafes, and Barkas area (Yemeni settlement) serve 100% halal meat as a matter of course. Halal meat is the default, not the exception. You will have no difficulty finding halal options across all cuisines - from biryani and haleem to mandi, kebabs, and traditional breakfast spots. Most Muslim-run establishments have served halal meat for generations.
best_options: Bade Miyan Kababs (Necklace Road - 4th generation halal)
tips: Old City (Charminar area) is the halal food heartland - almost every establishment serves halal meat by default
Irani cafes throughout the city universally serve halal meat - it's part of their identity
During Ramzan, the entire city transforms with Iftar-special menus and all-night halal dining - it's the best time to visit
Haleem during Ramzan is universally halal and is a communal tradition - no verification needed
If in doubt, simply ask 'Is this halal?' - staff at Muslim-run establishments will confirm proudly
Barkas area (Yemeni settlement) has authentic halal mandi restaurants like Kholani's Mandi
Avoid Paradise Biryani - despite being halal, locals consistently rate it as overrated and bland
Friday is the best day for special items - Shikhampur Kebab at Shadab, Bagara Khana with Dalcha
Most traditional breakfast spots (Paya, Nihari) open at 4-5 AM and sell out by 9 AM - go early
Cash is preferred at many Old City establishments - carry enough

strict_vegetarian.situation: Hyderabad is excellent for strict vegetarians with a thriving pure veg restaurant scene, particularly in areas like Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, Himayath Nagar, and Kukatpally. The city has everything from heritage Udupi restaurants (Taj Mahal Hotel since 1948) to modern pure veg fine dining (Tatva, Sattvam). South Indian breakfast culture is entirely vegetarian, and thali restaurants are abundant. The only challenge is in the Old City (Charminar area) where almost everything is non-veg - Anand Bhavan is the sole pure veg option there.

vegan_traveller.situation: Being vegan in Hyderabad requires more effort than being vegetarian, as dairy (ghee, butter, curd, cream) is used liberally in most dishes. Veganism as a concept is not widely understood - you will need to explain your requirements explicitly ('no milk, no butter, no ghee, no curd'). However, several restaurants now offer genuine vegan options, and South Indian breakfast staples like idli and plain dosa can be made vegan by specifying 'no ghee.' Gaurang's Kitchen stands out with a dedicated vegan thali. Modern cafes in Jubilee Hills and Banjara Hills are more likely to understand vegan requirements.
best_options: Gaurang's Kitchen (Jubilee Hills - dedicated vegan thali, rare in Hyderabad)
Tatva (Jubilee Hills - vegan options in fine dining)

tips: Gaurang's Kitchen is the standout - one of the few restaurants in Hyderabad with a dedicated vegan thali option

Veganism is not widely understood - use the phrase 'no milk, no butter, no ghee, no curd' for clarity

breakfast.local_style: Start your day the Hyderabadi way with either the iconic non-veg breakfast trio of Khichdi-Khatta-Keema or Paya-Naan, or dive into South Indian tiffin culture with butter dosas, idli, and vada at legendary bandis (food carts). Don't miss Irani Chai with Osmania biscuits - it's a morning ritual, not just a drink.
best_spots: Hotel Nayaab (Charminar) - Nihari with Char-Koni Naan + Bheja Fry, Rs 100-200 per person
Shah Ghouse (Shalibanda) - Khichdi + Keema Khatta (legendary breakfast combo), Rs 500 for two
Moosa Bhai Nihari Paya (Hussaini Alam) - 120-year-old Nalli Nihari recipe, bring your own bread
Alpha Hotel (Secunderabad) - Keema Roti + Special Tea, 68-year heritage, Rs 80-120
Govind Dosa (Charminar) - Butter Dosa + Tawa Idli, 40-year heritage, Rs 100-200 for two
Ram Ki Bandi (Nampally) - Pizza Dosa + Tawa Idli, opens 3:30 AM, Rs 150-250 for two
Nimrah Cafe (Charminar) - Irani Chai + Osmania Biscuits with Charminar view, Rs 20-50
Pragathi Tiffins (Koti) - Heritage idli and dosa, Rs 200 for two
Grand Hotel (Abids) - Bun Maskas + Irani Chai, 90-year heritage since 1935
breakfast.timing: Best enjoyed 5:00 AM - 9:00 AM. Many legendary spots sell out by 8-10 AM (especially Paya, Nihari, and Govind Dosa). Arrive early!

lunch.local_style: Lunch in Hyderabad is all about biryani - the undisputed king of midday meals. The authentic way is to eat mutton biryani at a legendary Old City or Panjagutta institution between 12-1:30 PM when the freshest batch is served. For vegetarians, unlimited thalis on banana leaves or elaborate Satvik buffets offer incredible variety and value.
best_spots: Meridian Restaurant (Panjagutta) - Mutton Biryani (locals' #1), 12-1:30 PM for freshest batch, Rs 250-400 per plate
Hotel Shadab (Charminar) - Mutton Biryani + Qubani ka Meetha, go upstairs for AC seating, Rs 200-350
Cafe Bahar (Basheer Bagh) - Chicken/Mutton Biryani, 50-year consistency, Rs 200-400

Chutneys (Multiple) - South Indian Tiffins/Thali with 6 varieties of chutneys, Rs 400-500 for two
Ishtaa (Hitech City) - Unlimited South Indian Thali on banana leaf, served only at lunch, Rs 500+
Taj Mahal Hotel / Dakshina Mandapa (Abids) - Heritage pure veg buffet with live dosa counter, Rs 850-1,200 for two
lunch.timing: 12:00 PM - 1:30 PM is the golden window for the freshest biryani. Vegetarian thalis are available 12:00-3:00 PM.

dinner.local_style: Dinner is when Hyderabad's diverse culinary traditions shine - from stone-cooked Pathar ka Gosht and smoky kebabs in the Old City to Arabian mandi with floor seating and upscale pure veg fine dining in Jubilee Hills. End with Khubani ka Meetha or Double ka Meetha for the quintessential Hyderabadi finish.
best_spots: Bade Miyan Kababs (Necklace Road) - Pathar ka Gosht + Sheekh Kebab with Hussain Sagar lake breeze, since 1954, Rs 500 for two
Chicha's (Lakdikapul) - Pathar ka Gosht + Bheja Fry (daily availability), assorted kebab platter, Rs 1,000 for two
Hotel Shadab (Charminar) - Mutton Biryani + Boti Kebab + Qubani ka Meetha, legendary 30+ year institution

Aazebo (Multiple) - Mutton Mafdoon Mandi (weekends), Al Faham Chicken Mandi, Rs 1,000-1,500 for two
Tatva (Jubilee Hills) - Smoked Paneer Pesto Tikka + fine dining thali, Hyderabad's first pure veg fine dining, Rs 1,900 for two
Gaurang's Kitchen (Jubilee Hills) - Unlimited Gujarati/Rajasthani Thali, dedicated Jain and vegan thalis available, Rs 2,000 for two
Kebab-E-Jahangiri (Charminar) - Sheekh Kebab + Warqi Paratha, under Rs 100 for a full meal, 36+ year institution
Grand Hotel (Abids) - Tangdi Chicken + Fish Chilli + Falooda, 90-year heritage, open until 1 AM
dinner.timing: 7:00 PM - 10:30 PM is the prime dinner window. Old City kebab spots open at 4 PM and sell out by 9 PM. Fine dining restaurants take last orders by 10:30-11:00 PM.

late_night.options: Hyderabad has one of India's best late-night food scenes. Shah Ghouse Tolichowki serves biryani until 4 AM and the 2 AM crowd is legendary. Grand Hotel (Abids) stays open until 1 AM. Ohri's Eatmor is a reliable 24/7 buffet option. Ram Ki Bandi's Hitech City outlet serves dosas until midnight. During Ramzan, the entire Old City transforms into an all-night food festival with haleem, paya, and biryani available from 3 AM onwards.

extreme_budget.description: Under INR 100 for a full meal

Any Karachi Bakery outlet (Banjara Hills, Hitec City, etc.)
